questions.q: What are the two most common accounting-triggering actions in Payables, as described in this lesson?
options: Creating a supplier record and updating a bank account
Invoice validation and payment
Running a report and exporting a spreadsheet
Setting up a new Chart of Accounts
questions.explain: Invoice validation raises an Invoices event, and payment raises a separate Payments event, as the lesson describes.

questions.q: What does validating a Payables invoice represent, in accounting terms?
options: Cash leaving the company immediately
A supplier being deleted from the system
A customer receipt being applied
The recognition of a liability — the company now owes the supplier
questions.explain: Validating an invoice raises an event representing the liability owed to the supplier, separate from the later payment event.

questions.q: What are the equivalent triggers in Receivables to Payables' invoice validation and payment?
options: Creating a new customer and closing a ledger period
Invoice completion and receipt application
Running depreciation and asset retirement
Bank statement reconciliation
questions.explain: Invoice completion recognizes revenue and an amount due, while receipt application reduces the receivable and increases cash, mirroring AP's two triggers.

questions.q: What common pattern do both Payables and Receivables share, according to this lesson, regarding Draft and Final accounting?
options: Neither subledger ever uses Draft mode
Final mode always runs automatically immediately after every transaction
Draft and Final modes are identical in both subledgers with no distinction
Draft accounting commonly runs close to real time for visibility, while Final accounting is typically run on a schedule or on demand once transactions are settled
questions.explain: Both subledgers typically favor near-real-time Draft accounting for visibility and scheduled or on-demand Final accounting once transactions are settled.

questions.q: When would running Create Accounting manually, on demand, be most useful?
options: Never; manual runs are not supported in Oracle Fusion
Only during the very first day a company goes live, and never again
During implementation testing, period-end catch-up, and troubleshooting scenarios
Only for Fixed Assets, never for Payables or Receivables
questions.explain: Manual, on-demand runs of Create Accounting are especially useful during testing, catching up at period-end, and troubleshooting.
